questions.question: A man in his late 70s with a prior Lotus 27 mm valve implanted in 2014 and an Evolut 23 mm valve implanted in 2022 now presents with severe prosthetic stenosis (mean gradient 49 mm Hg) and grade 2–3 intraprosthetic regurgitation. His EuroSCORE II is 27 % and he has multiple comorbidities—including COPD, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease stage III, prior gastrointestinal bleeding episodes, three‑vessel coronary artery disease treated percutaneously, and a history of treated Enterococcus faecalis prosthetic‑valve endocarditis now resolved. Surgical explantation would require extensive aortic root reconstruction. Which clinical factors most strongly favor proceeding with a third transcatheter aortic‑valve implantation rather than surgical redo?

Explain the pathophysiologic mechanisms by which prosthetic‑valve endocarditis accelerates structural degeneration of bioprosthetic transcatheter valves leading to leaflet fibrosis, calcification and functional stenosis.

When planning a third transcatheter valve inside two previously implanted frames (Lotus + Evolut), which multidetector computed‑tomography measurements are most predictive of coronary‑obstruction risk, and what threshold values define a high‑risk anatomy?

Three months after his second TAVI the patient develops an increase in mean transvalvular gradient from ~20 mm Hg to >50 mm Hg together with new intraprosthetic regurgitation on echocardiography. List the principal differential diagnoses for prosthetic aortic‑valve dysfunction in this setting and indicate the key diagnostic test(s) that help discriminate each entity.

Echocardiography after the third intervention shows mean gradient 49 mm Hg, effective orifice area 0·5 cm² (indexed AVA 0·3 cm²/m²), and Doppler velocity index 0·24. According to Valve Academic Research Consortium‑3 criteria, how would you grade the severity of patient‑prosthesis mismatch and what are its major prognostic implications?

During deployment of an Acurate neo2 within the pre‑existing Evolut frame, how are commissural alignment and high implantation depth achieved? Specify the fluoroscopic views or CT‑derived landmarks used intra‑procedurally to ensure optimal positioning while preserving future coronary access.

For Enterococcus faecalis prosthetic‑valve endocarditis occurring after transcatheter aortic‑valve replacement, what is the guideline‑directed antimicrobial regimen—including choice of agents and minimum duration—and under what circumstances would lifelong suppressive antibiotics be considered?

After successful TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV implantation, outline an evidence‑based surveillance strategy over the first year—including timing of imaging studies (echocardiography ± CT), specific haemodynamic thresholds that would trigger further evaluation or reintervention, and any adjunctive clinical assessments.
